raw_response: Banks reported the FDIC special assessment as a notable item that significantly impacted expense comparisons. In the fourth quarter of 2023, one bank noted that reported expenses were down 16% year-over-year primarily due to the FDIC special assessment recorded in the prior year's fourth quarter, while another bank included a $1.9 billion FDIC special assessment in its 2023 non-interest expense total. For 2024, banks indicated that if the assessment was finalized in the fourth quarter of 2023 or incurred in early 2024, it would increase expected expenses; specifically, one bank noted that excluding this item, 2023 expenses were $53.6 billion, and another stated that its full-year 2024 non-interest expense guidance remained unchanged despite the assessment being included in first-quarter results.
